0.0.n: A compound noun combining 毒, poison, and ガス, gas.

0.1.n: Part of かもしれません, an expression indicating uncertainty.

0.2.n: The polite negative form of 知れる completes かもしれません; interpret the whole expression as possibility.

1.0.n: The owner is unstated; here it refers to your own mouth.

1.1.n: Lists examples rather than a complete set, linking 口 and 鼻 here.

1.2.n: Paired with 口 as another place the gas must not enter.

1.3.n: Marks the destination of entry, applying to both 口 and 鼻.

1.4.n: The plain negative form of 入る is used before ようにする.

1.5.n: Following a negative verb, よう helps describe an outcome to prevent.

1.6.n: Links よう to する, forming a pattern for taking care to achieve or prevent something.

1.7.n: The plain form ends this instruction; with 入らないように, it tells you to prevent entry.

2.0.n: Names one route by which the gas could enter your body.

2.1.n: Marks 口 as the destination of 入る.

2.2.n: 入っ is the changed form of 入る used before たり; 入ったり lists an example action.

2.3.n: Lists entry into the mouth as one possible event; no second たり appears here.

2.5.n: A plain-form verb; the gas being inhaled is understood rather than stated.

2.6.n: Introduces the consequence of the gas entering your mouth or being inhaled.

2.8.n: Refers to your body and, by extension, your health.

2.9.n: Marks what is affected by 悪い: your body.

2.10.n: With 体に, this adjective describes a negative effect on health.

2.11.n: In ことがある, it refers to cases when the preceding statement is true.

2.12.n: Marks こと as what exists in the expression ことがあります.

2.13.n: The polite form of ある; with こと, it indicates that something sometimes happens or can happen.

3.0.n: A general noun, not the name of a particular structure.

3.1.n: Connects 建物 to 中 to identify the interior of the building.

3.2.n: A location noun used with 建物の to specify the building’s interior.

3.3.n: Marks the location where someone is present, used with いる.

3.4.n: Used for the presence of people or animals; here the unstated subject is you.

3.5.n: After いる, it identifies the time or situation in which the instruction applies.

3.6.n: Sets being inside a building as the situation this instruction addresses.

3.8.n: Names the destination; the movement verb is left unstated.

3.9.n: Marks a direction; here 外へ implies an instruction to go outside.

4.0.n: Names the location where you already are before following the instruction.

4.1.n: Marks 外 as the location of the person described by いる.

4.2.n: Describes someone’s presence outdoors and directly modifies とき.

4.3.n: Turns 外にいる into a description of the situation in which to act.

4.4.n: Highlights being outdoors as the situation addressed, contrasting with the previous indoor instruction.

4.6.n: The noun names what is doing the blowing.

4.7.n: Identifies 風 as the subject of 吹いてくる.

4.8.n: The て-form of 吹く plus くる describes wind approaching from a direction.

4.9.n: Modified by 風が吹いてくる, it means the direction the wind comes from, not where it goes.

4.10.n: Connects the wind’s source direction with 高いところ, locating the higher ground on that side.

4.11.n: Directly modifies ところ and refers to ground elevation here.

4.12.n: With 高い, it describes elevated ground as the escape destination.

4.13.n: Marks the destination of escape: elevated ground in the direction the wind comes from.

4.14.n: The plain form functions as a direct safety instruction rather than a description of someone’s actions.

0.tip: Treat かもしれません as one polite expression meaning that something might be true.

1.lit: Make sure it does not enter the mouth or nose.
1.tip: A negative verb plus ようにする tells you to take care to prevent something.

2.lit: If it enters the mouth or is inhaled, there are occasions when it is bad for the body.
2.tip: ことがあります after a description means it can be true in some cases, rather than always.

3.lit: When inside a building, toward outside.
3.tip: Japanese instructions can omit the movement verb when a destination plus へ makes the intended action clear.

4.lit: When outside, flee toward a high place in the direction from which the wind comes blowing.
4.tip: 風が吹いてくる方 means the direction the wind comes from: go upwind, not downwind.
